I am an old man, 84 years, and I have farmed this land my whole life the way my father showed me. This maize plot is small, less than one acre, and I plant beans between the maize like always — that way if one fails the other feeds us. I have some cattle, so I carry their manure to the field before the rains; that is what I trust, not the powder from the shop that costs money I do not have. My sons and grandchildren help me now because my back is not strong, and I save my seed from last harvest like I have always done.
